title: Classical Foundations and Genomic Advances in Human Pigmentation and Hair Morphology
content: Pigmentation and hair morphology are both among the earliest visible traits studied in the context of human heredity and genetics. Over the past 100+ years, both traits have been defined in various ways and their genetic underpinnings have been studied across major methodological approaches in the field to varying degrees of success. Here we review what can be learned from the divergent trajectories of genetic research on these two traits, particularly about how phenotypic definitions shape connections between genetic findings, biological mechanisms, and measured variation. We consider how a new era of functional genomics may integrate these bodies of knowledge, and to move forward our understanding of complex traits, for which pigmentation and hair morphology provide two illustrative models.
